description: Width tiers for Visual Arts — Years 5–6
subject: Visual Arts

width_notes.minimum: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Years 5–6, minimum is a planned or documented making or exploring act that demonstrates intentional use of visual conventions.
width_notes.typical: Full descriptor scope — deliberate planning, documentation and reflection across multiple materials, forms and cultural contexts.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment through additional contexts: cross-arts connections, digital/physical combinations, First Nations directions, social or political themes. Adds new contexts, not higher difficulty.

AC9AVA6C01.minimum_width: Use at least two visual conventions and one planned process to create an artwork that communicates an intended idea, perspective or meaning.
AC9AVA6C01.typical_width: Plan and create artworks using combinations of visual conventions, processes and materials (including analog and digital); make and document intentional choices; communicate aesthetic qualities, ideas and meaning; experiment with framing, composition and hybrid materials.
wider: Create an artwork that combines at least one digital and one analog material — document findings in a logbook and explain how each material contributes to the communicative intent
Explore modular patterns using grid paper or digital systems (glyphs, pixels, shapes) — transform the grid into a different form such as a poster or printmaking template

Investigate and apply structural approaches used by First Nations Australian artists in textiles, design or public artworks — with guidance from culturally authoritative resources, explore how visual conventions communicate cultural knowledge
elaborations: applying their understanding of visual arts processes and materials to create artworks that are both robust and communicate intended aesthetic qualities
using visual conventions and visual arts processes to communicate ideas and meaning in their artwork; for example, exploring the ways that different brushstrokes can communicate meaning in a painting
examining a series of diverse artworks that employ frames, windows, mirrors or sections as containers or portals into space
trying and testing a range of analog visual arts materials, such as paints, drawing materials or clay, and comparing virtual simulations of these materials
creating artworks that are the product of ideas they have developed through experimentation and planning
forming modular patterns, images or letters with grid paper or an online digital system to combine glyphs, pixels and shapes

AC9AVA6D01.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one visual arts process; document what was tried, what worked and what was noticed.
AC9AVA6D01.typical_width: Experiment with, document and reflect on ways to use a range of visual conventions, processes and materials; use Viewpoints questions to extend thinking; explore printmaking, 3D hand-building, gesture drawing, Augmented Reality face filters and cross-arts visual mapping.
wider: Map the movements of a dance sequence using visual conventions — represent shapes, levels, directions and energies as an abstract visual artwork, and reflect on how colour and composition communicate mood

Explore Augmented Reality face filters — identify key asset types, create a digital or analog concept for a filter that communicates an intended concept, consider how it could be used in a performance context
Explore 3D hand-building using earthenware or modelling clay — develop surface decoration techniques and reflect on how form and surface communicate ideas
elaborations: drawing on themes they are learning about in other subjects and visually brainstorming a range of diverse ideas that link to this theme
using visual conventions and visual arts processes to map the movements of a dance sequence
presenting a selection of Augmented Reality face filters that map and track the face in real time
exploring a range of approaches to printmaking, such as transferring previously created drawings onto printing foam and creating multiple prints that explore visual conventions
making informed choices about using various combinations of representational elements appropriate for a concept or subject matter
exploring different approaches to working in 3D forms, such as developing a range of techniques in modelling using materials such as earthenware clay or modelling clay

AC9AVA6E01.minimum_width: Explore one artwork from a different culture, time or place; identify how visual conventions, processes and materials are combined to communicate an idea or perspective.
AC9AVA6E01.typical_width: Explore how visual conventions, processes and materials are combined to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning across a range of cultures, times and places; examine multiple perspectives on the same artwork; investigate how Australian and international artists express historical, social and environmental concerns.
wider: Compare how different artists present multiple perspectives on the colonisation of Australia — examine works from First Nations Australian, British and other perspectives; discuss how artworks develop social awareness
Explore artworks from countries or regions in Asia that communicate a topic relevant to class — individually express your own view in a series of sequential visual panels without text

Listen to audio descriptions of artworks by Australian artists in Australian institutions — create your own audio description of a selected work, considering what is essential for a visually impaired audience
elaborations: investigating how a diverse range of Australian artists have expressed historical, social and environmental concerns over time
identifying ways that artworks by different artists can present multiple perspectives of the same event, discussing how these works can assist the development of social awareness
exploring a range of Australian and international artworks, such as artworks from countries or regions in Asia, that communicate a topic or issue the class is learning about in another subject
using Viewpoints to develop questions to examine, compare and contrast what they notice in an artwork
examining audio descriptions as an accessible way for people with impaired vision to enjoy visual arts

AC9AVA6E02.minimum_width: Explore one artwork by a First Nations Australian artist that continues or revitalises culture; identify one way the artwork communicates identity, story or cultural knowledge.
AC9AVA6E02.typical_width: Explore ways that First Nations Australian artists use visual arts to continue and revitalise cultures — investigate site-specific works, murals, street art and installations; examine how artworks serve multiple purposes (cultural practice, narrative, identity declaration); use Viewpoints to deepen questioning.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian artists and designers use textiles, fashion and other applied forms to share cultural knowledge with the broader community — examine how visual conventions communicate meaning across contexts
Explore representations of First Nations Australians as superheroes in comics and popular culture — investigate how artists embed community and identity in popular visual forms
Investigate site-specific works by First Nations Australian artists — explore how the site itself shapes the meaning of the work and how cultural knowledge is communicated through placement and form
elaborations: exploring the ways that a diverse range of First Nations Australian artists embed themselves and their communities in artworks in a range of representative forms as a visual declaration of identity, storytelling and resilience
exploring the ways that visual arts created by First Nations Australians may have multiple purposes; for example, art as cultural practice, art to communicate cultural understandings, or as narrative
investigating a range of site-specific artworks created by First Nations Australian artists, exploring how they communicate and celebrate cultural knowledge and understandings
using Viewpoints to question understandings about artists and artworks

investigating how meaning and purpose are communicated in artworks and design created or co-created by First Nations Australians; for example, learning about how visual conventions are used in artworks and designs, such as textiles and fashion, to share cultural knowledge with the broader community

AC9AVA6P01.minimum_width: Select and arrange documentation of at least one aspect of their visual arts practice and present it in an informal or formal setting with a brief explanation.
AC9AVA6P01.typical_width: Select and present documentation of visual arts practice and artworks in informal and formal settings; prepare artworks for physical display; create labels, artist statements and exhibition materials; explore digital and QR-coded methods of sharing; work collaboratively on online exhibitions.
wider: Develop a complete set of exhibition materials — labels, an exhibition introduction, advertising and a review — for a class exhibition of student works

Explore Augmented Reality to place collage, objects or forms in physical space as a digital layer — produce a short moving image work that maps how visual assets change depending on audience point of view
Explore options for sharing work in public spaces (café galleries, community arts events) — plan and document what would need to change about the work and its presentation to suit a public audience
elaborations: preparing artworks for display within the school environment; for example, measuring and making frames or stands for artworks, using repurposed/recycled materials
exploring digital methods of encoding information in artworks to share with audiences; for example, by using image coding software or QR codes
working collaboratively to create an online exhibition of student work
exploring options for sharing work in public spaces; for example, in café galleries, public exhibition spaces or through community arts events
selecting and arranging evidence of their learning from their investigations, experiments and reflections in a way that communicates the development of their ideas and understandings
considering artworks that represent a spatial awareness in digital or physical forms; for example, experimenting with Augmented Reality to place collage, objects or forms in space
creating a set of art labels to accompany artworks in a class exhibition of student work
